settings.title: Traditional Chinese practice
settings.text: Known as lóng xuè jié, used for centuries in southern China to support healing.

settings.title: 18th century
settings.text: Dissolved into the varnish that gave Italian violins their famous red glow.

settings.title: Today
settings.text: Studied and prized in modern skincare for its protective, soothing properties.

settings.title: Forms a "second skin"
settings.text: On application it creates a breathable protective film that shields against the elements.

settings.title: Rich in antioxidants
settings.text: Naturally occurring flavonoids help defend skin against everyday oxidative stress.

settings.title: Supports collagen
settings.text: Studied for its role in supporting the collagen that keeps skin firm and smooth.

settings.title: Calms visible redness
settings.text: Known for its soothing effect on stressed, sensitised or irritated-looking skin.

settings.title: Locks in moisture
settings.text: Helps reduce water loss so skin stays hydrated and comfortable for longer.
